mainEntity.name: What kitchen tools do I need if I am setting up a new kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: A vegetable peeler, a chopper or a good knife, a cutting board, a spatula and a pair of tongs. These five tools cover daily cooking from breakfast to dinner. Add a whisk if you bake and a grater if you cook with fresh ginger or garlic regularly. Buy the basics first, cook with them for a few weeks, then add what you find yourself missing. A full set bought upfront often includes tools that sit unused.

mainEntity.name: Which kitchen tool material lasts the longest?

acceptedAnswer.text: Stainless steel. It resists rust, handles high heat, cleans easily and holds up to years of daily use. Silicone is the second most durable and the safest option for non-stick cookware. Bamboo and wood last well with proper care but need occasional oiling to prevent cracking. Nylon is the least durable but works fine as a budget option for light cooking.

mainEntity.name: Can I use metal kitchen tools on non-stick pans?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Metal spatulas, tongs and spoons scratch non-stick coatings and shorten the life of your pan. Use silicone or nylon tools on any non-stick surface. Stainless steel and cast iron cookware can handle metal utensils without damage.

mainEntity.name: How often should I replace my kitchen tools?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the material and how often you use them. Stainless steel tools can last five to ten years with proper care. Silicone tools last three to five years before they start showing wear. Wooden spoons and bamboo boards need replacing when they crack, splinter or develop deep grooves that trap food. Nylon tools wear fastest and usually need replacing every one to two years.

Title Default Title Add to cart 1 2 3 Next Choosing the right kitchen tools for how you cook The right tools depend on what you cook, how often and how much prep your meals need. Pick based on your actual routine, not a checklist someone else wrote. Before adding anything to your kitchen, consider these: 1. How often you cook - daily home cooks need durable, comfortable tools that handle repetitive tasks. Weekend cooks can get away with fewer, multi-purpose options 2. What you cook most - roti, paratha and chapati cooking calls for rolling pins, tongs and flat spatulas. Salad and fruit prep needs sharp peelers, graters and a reliable cutting board 3. Your cookware type - non-stick pans need silicone or nylon tools that will not scratch the coating. Stainless steel or cast iron cookware works fine with metal utensils 4. Counter and drawer space - compact kitchens benefit from multi-functional gadgets and stackable tools that do not crowd your workspace. Materials that matter in kitchen tools The material of a kitchen tool decides how long it lasts, how it feels in your hand and what cookware it can safely touch. Most kitchens end up with a mix of materials because no single one does everything. 1. Stainless steel - the most durable option. Rust-resistant, easy to clean, handles high heat and lasts for years. Best for knives, graters, tongs and ladles. Heavier than other materials but built to take daily use without wearing down 2. Silicone (food-grade, BPA-free) - heat-resistant up to 230°C, flexible and safe for non-stick surfaces. Best for spatulas, whisks, tongs and ice cube trays. Will not scratch coated cookware and cleans up fast 3. Bamboo and wood - lightweight, naturally antibacterial and gentle on knife edges. Best for cutting boards, spoons and stirring tools. Needs occasional oiling to prevent cracking but ages well with proper care 4. Nylon and ABS plastic - affordable and safe for non-stick pans. Lighter than steel but wears out faster. Good for budget-friendly starter sets and everyday stirring tools Kitchen tools for food prep Prep takes up more time than actual cooking in most Pakistani kitchens. The right prep tools cut that time down and keep the process safer. 1. Peelers - Y-peelers and swivel peelers handle potatoes, carrots, apples and cucumbers. Look for ergonomic handles if you peel large batches regularly 2. Graters and zesters - box graters cover ginger, cheese and vegetables in one tool. Flat graters and zesters work better for fine grating like garlic and lemon zest 3. Choppers - manual choppers dice onions, tomatoes and herbs in seconds. A push chopper or pull-string chopper saves time when you are prepping for a large meal 4. Cutting boards - the surface you prep on matters. Stainless steel boards are hygienic and easy to sanitize. Bamboo boards are lighter and kinder to your knife edges. Kitchen tools for cutting and slicing A good knife changes how you cook. The right blade makes cutting faster, safer and more precise. - Chef knives - the all-rounder. Handles vegetables, meat, herbs and fruit. A 6 to 8 inch blade covers most home cooking needs - Paring knives - small, precise blades for peeling, trimming and detailed work - Kitchen scissors - multi-blade herb scissors cut coriander and spring onions without a board. Poultry shears handle bone and cartilage that regular scissors cannot - Knife accessories - sharpeners, honing rods, blade guards and magnetic holders keep your edges sharp and your storage safe. Kitchen tools for cooking and serving Once the prep is done, cooking tools take over. These are the things you reach for at the stove, over the pan, at the serving table. a. Spatulas and turners - silicone spatulas flex into bowls and scrape cleanly. Flat turners flip eggs, parathas and fish without breaking them apart b. Tongs - locking tongs with silicone tips grip food securely without scratching non-stick surfaces. Essential for flipping, tossing and plating c. Whisks - balloon whisks blend eggs, batters and sauces evenly. Flat whisks work better for gravies and roux in shallow pans d. Ladles, skimmers and slotted spoons - stainless steel options last longest. Nylon works if you cook primarily in non-stick. Taking care of your kitchen tools Good tools last years with basic maintenance. Poor care shortens the life of even the most durable products. 1. Dry after washing - most damage comes from tools sitting wet. Stainless steel develops water spots. Bamboo boards warp and crack if left soaking 2. Sharpen knives regularly - a dull blade needs more force and causes more injuries than a sharp one. Use a honing rod weekly and a sharpener every few months 3. Oil wooden and bamboo tools - food-grade mineral oil prevents drying, cracking and splitting. Apply once a month for boards that get heavy use 4. Store blades safely - knife holders, magnetic strips or blade guards protect both the edge and your fingers. Loose blades in a drawer are a safety hazard 5. Check silicone for wear - silicone tools are low-maintenance but inspect them periodically. Cracks or tears mean it is time to replace. How to pick kitchen tools that will not end up unused Not every kitchen gadget earns its place. The difference between a useful tool and a drawer filler comes down to three things: Frequency - if you cannot see yourself using it at least twice a week, skip it. A garlic press you use daily is worth it. A melon baller you use once a year is not Multi-purpose value - tools that handle more than one job save both money and space. Kitchen scissors that cut herbs, open packages and trim meat are more practical than three separate tools Comfort - ergonomic handles, non-slip grips and balanced weight matter when you use a tool for 20 minutes straight. Test how it feels, not just how it looks. Why buy kitchen tools and gadgets online from Wehome? Every product on the store is quality-tested before listing. No bulk-import dumps. No untested inventory. The collection spans eight subcategories covering prep, cooking, cutting and organizing, so you can equip your kitchen without jumping between five different stores. - Cash on delivery across Pakistan - Free shipping on orders above Rs. 2,500 - WhatsApp support for replacements and questions - Quality-first selection with each product reviewed before it goes live. Read more ▾ Frequently Asked Questions What kitchen tools do I need if I am setting up a new kitchen? A vegetable peeler, a chopper or a good knife, a cutting board, a spatula and a pair of tongs. These five tools cover daily cooking from breakfast to dinner. Add a whisk if you bake and a grater if you cook with fresh ginger or garlic regularly. Buy the basics first, cook with them for a few weeks, then add what you find yourself missing. A full set bought upfront often includes tools that sit unused. Which kitchen tool material lasts the longest? Stainless steel. It resists rust, handles high heat, cleans easily and holds up to years of daily use. Silicone is the second most durable and the safest option for non-stick cookware. Bamboo and wood last well with proper care but need occasional oiling to prevent cracking. Nylon is the least durable but works fine as a budget option for light cooking. Can I use metal kitchen tools on non-stick pans? No. Metal spatulas, tongs and spoons scratch non-stick coatings and shorten the life of your pan. Use silicone or nylon tools on any non-stick surface. Stainless steel and cast iron cookware can handle metal utensils without damage. How often should I replace my kitchen tools? It depends on the material and how often you use them. Stainless steel tools can last five to ten years with proper care. Silicone tools last three to five years before they start showing wear. Wooden spoons and bamboo boards need replacing when they crack, splinter or develop deep grooves that trap food. Nylon tools wear fastest and usually need replacing every one to two years. Its lightweight handheld design makes personal cooling easy without carrying a bulky electric fan. If you’re comparing the portable fan price in Pakistan , this mini USB fan offers a practical combination of portability, rechargeable operation and adjustable airflow. The fan is designed for everyday personal cooling and can be conveniently charged through a compatible USB power source. Its compact body fits easily into a handbag, backpack, desk drawer or travel bag, making it useful during Pakistan’s warm summer weather, daily commutes and situations where you need a personal breeze. Why Choose This Portable Hand Fan? A conventional fan is useful when you are sitting in one place, but a portable hand fan gives you cooling wherever you move. This rechargeable mini fan is suitable for: Home and bedroom use Office work Studying and online classes Travel and commuting Outdoor activities Shopping and walking Events and gatherings Desk and workstation use Personal cooling during hot weather Its small size makes it particularly useful when you don’t want to carry a full-size fan. Rechargeable USB Design The fan uses a rechargeable power system, allowing you to use it without keeping it connected to a wall outlet during operation. When the battery needs charging, connect the fan to a compatible USB power source. You can conveniently charge it using compatible devices such as: USB power adapters Power banks Laptops Desktop computers Other suitable USB charging sources This makes the portable rechargeable fan convenient for travel, office use and everyday personal cooling. Charging note: Actual charging time and battery runtime depend on the battery specification, charging source and selected operating speed. Check the product label or included instructions for the exact electrical specifications. Three Adjustable Speed Settings Different situations require different airflow levels. The fan’s three-speed design allows you to select the airflow level that feels most comfortable. Low Speed Suitable for gentle airflow while working, reading or studying. Medium Speed A balanced setting for everyday indoor personal cooling. High Speed Useful when you need stronger airflow during warmer conditions or outdoor use. Having multiple speed settings makes the fan more versatile than a basic single-speed handheld fan. Compact Handheld Design The biggest advantage of this mini portable fan is its compact form. You can easily carry it in: A handbag Backpack School bag Laptop bag Travel luggage Office drawer Its lightweight construction makes it convenient for everyday use without adding unnecessary bulk. Bladeless Fan Design The product uses a bladeless-style airflow design , providing a different experience from traditional exposed-blade handheld fans. The enclosed airflow design gives the fan a clean, modern appearance and makes it comfortable to hold while using it for personal cooling. Because this is a compact personal fan rather than a room air conditioner, it is designed to provide localized airflow , not cool an entire room. That distinction is important when choosing the right fan for your needs. Multiple Colour Options The Classic Portable USB Mini Fan is available in multiple colours , allowing you to choose the option that best matches your personal style. Because colours may vary according to stock availability, the exact colour supplied may depend on the selected variant. Portable Fan for Pakistan’s Summer Hot weather can make everyday activities uncomfortable, particularly when you’re travelling, studying, working or spending time outdoors. A compact portable fan in Pakistan can provide personal airflow exactly where you need it. It is especially practical for: 1.Students Keep a personal cooling solution nearby during study sessions, online classes and homework. 2.Office Workers Use it at your workstation when you need additional airflow without taking up the space of a conventional fan. 4.Travellers Its compact design makes it easy to carry during road trips, commuting and holidays. 5.Outdoor Users Take it with you when attending outdoor events, walking, shopping or spending time outside. 6.Home Users Keep it beside your bed, sofa, study table or workspace for convenient personal cooling. Portable Fan During Load Shedding A rechargeable fan can also be useful when conventional mains-powered cooling is unavailable. Once charged, the fan can provide personal airflow without needing to remain connected to a wall socket.
